lastText: ☰⚙File ClosedThe Raids Not FlownContestedThe War Cabinet and Chiefs of Staff, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. The February 1945 eastern-city raids were declined: Dresden never becomes the word it became, and the oil and rail campaigns finished the war's arithmetic without it, exactly as their own advocates' logic implied they could. The Scheldt was cleared before the autumn's offensives rather than after: Antwerp opened weeks early, and the priority error most postwar assessments rank among the campaign's costliest was simply not made. The fleet was kept at Alexandria while Crete fell, the cruisers saved and the Army left to remember it: the island fell in days, with a large part of the garrison taken prisoner.
